gates.sentence: Inventory and preservation baseline recorded: pinned HEAD, every tab and control enumerated, frontend handler to API route map, backend authorization trace, baseline screenshots and test results, owner-approved preservation matrix. No redesign before this.
Design tokens, navigation shell, shared status/evidence components and accessible overlays exist with no route or capability change and with keyboard coverage.
Start and Chat journeys are usable end to end, including empty, loading, streaming, error and recovery states, with an explicit Chat-to-Harness handoff.
Harness and Pipeline surface durable task state, approvals, diffs, artifacts and pause/cancel/resume/recovery without inventing client-side state.
Council and Compare present participants, stages, disagreement and measured provenance without collapsing the two workflows into one.
Cross-tab consistency and accessibility/responsive regression are demonstrated: keyboard walks, screen-reader labels, touch targets, bounded SSE rendering.
Automated preservation end-to-end tests, adversarial permission/recovery UI tests, full screenshot review, README/onboarding verification and a release gate with a handover report.

known_regressions.regression: The demo path's usage line still reports fabricated tok/s figures (29.5 / 42.1) and `record_perf` still stores them, because the flag the pane now reads (`demo`) does not stop the write; the pane no longer draws a figure for a demo reply, but the perf samples and the throughput card still count it. Recorded as an open risk for the runtime program rather than fixed inside a UI pull request.

`syncUnifiedSelectors` rebuilds the seat pickers from the catalogue, which lists only resident local models; loading a model can therefore re-pick a seat whose model was not in the catalogue. The row stays true to what the round would post, but the operator's earlier choice can change under them.

A pipeline view restored from the browser's checkpoint has no contract: the checkpoint stores what each seat produced (content, reasoning, usage), not what it was allowed, so the `Allowed` column reads `-` after a reload. Absence is drawn as absence rather than filled in, but the fix is to widen the checkpoint payload, which belongs to the recovery story that owns that format.

The four Hall seat pickers are rewritten by a readiness refresh while a round runs: after the round the selectors can name models that did not answer (a cloud alias rather than the local models the summons posted). The verdict table is unaffected - it names the model each stored message carries - and the walk re-selects the models before its capture, but the pickers disagreeing with the transcript is a real defect this story found and did not fix; it belongs to the readiness refresh that rewrites them.

Shared wording is a lexical measure: a seat that makes the same point in different words reads as `not in the decision` and is named under Dissent. The block says so in its basis line and prints the percentage, so a reader can discount it, but the pane cannot tell disagreement from paraphrasing and does not claim to.

A comparison runs with `auto_unload: true`, so the local model it just compared can leave the catalogue: the checkbox strip is rebuilt from telemetry and stops offering it, while its card and its row stay on screen. The result is honest but confusing on a screenshot, and it is the picker's refresh behaviour (recorded under P4-01) rather than this story's; the walk's captures clip the run line, panels and results for that reason.

The server has no per-panel error event: one provider exception ends the whole `run_stages` run, so a failed comparison always leaves the panels behind it `not run` rather than failing one and carrying on. The pane says exactly that and does not pretend to have a partial panel failure it cannot observe.

Three of the ten states cannot be produced by the app in this environment: `queued` appears only between the click and the first `panel_start`, `empty` needs a runtime that finishes without words, and `stream ended` needs a socket that drops mid-run. They are asserted in the pane's vocabulary and in the inventory, and the fixture can produce six of the ten (answered, cut, demo, failed, stopped, not-run).

`ttft` is the runtime's first-token figure for the stage as `app.py` computed it; for the fixture it is 0.04 s for every reply because the stand-in runtime sends `time_to_first_token: 0.04`. Nothing in the pane rounds or invents it, but a reader should not read the fixture's equal numbers as equal hardware.

`prefill_tps` and `cached_tokens` travel in the usage object and are deliberately not printed: the pane has no reader for them that would not be a row of zeroes (the local path always sends `prefill_tps: 0.0`, `cached_tokens: 0`). They stay in the payload for a later story rather than being drawn as measured zeros.

A demo reply still writes the invented 29.5 / 42.1 tok/s to `perf_samples` through `record_perf`; the pane no longer draws them anywhere, but the store still receives them, and that write belongs to the runtime program (recorded since P4-01).

The arbiter's figures are the judge model's, so in the fixture they equal the panel's when the judge is the first model. That is the fixture answering one model the same way twice, not the pane echoing a row.

The browser's copy restores the comparison, not the run: the model checkboxes are rebuilt from the live strip, so a restored comparison whose models the runtime has since unloaded comes back with those models listed in its cards (correct) but not ticked (also correct, and stated on the bar) - pressing Start would compare something else, which the bar says in as many words.
`Forget this copy` is per browser: another browser or profile still holds its own copy of the same run, and the bar only ever speaks for this one.

The server's copy is the redacted export, so a comparison that happened to contain credential-shaped text comes back with that text replaced by the exporter. The bar and the markdown state this rather than pretending the read-back is byte-identical.

A demo reply still writes the invented 29.5 / 42.1 tok/s to `perf_samples` through `record_perf` (recorded since P4-01); the record bar restores a demo reply with the `demo` status and no figure, so the copy does not amplify it.

The copy cap can shorten the longest replies of a very large comparison; the bar states the number of characters dropped, but the dropped text is not recoverable from this browser - the server's copy, when there is one, is the complete one.

`stopped` carries the warn tone, where the Harness used to draw `CANCELLED` neutral. A stop is not a failure (that is `danger`) and it is not a normal completion either; the Panes now agree on one tone, and Compare - which already used warn - is unchanged.

Model-residency chips stay outside the vocabulary: `LOADED`/`LOADING` describe what a model is, not what a run did, and they are drawn as `badge` chips rather than the status component. The inventory lists them as a stated exception rather than folding them into a table whose meaning is 'where does this stand'.

A few counts keep their own words (`0 / 4 ready`, `2 ready · 1 configured`): the numbers are the value and the trailing word is the vocabulary's. The walk accepts a chip built from vocabulary words plus digits and separators, and fails on anything else.

`scripts/status_walk.mjs` still exercises the component with arbitrary words (`COMPLETED`/`FAILED` as literals in its own probe) because it is testing the writer, not the vocabulary; no pane draws those words any more.

A server state the vocabulary has never seen is shown as the server's own word. That is intentional - the alternative is a wrong word - but it means a new backend state reaches the reader before the table learns its name.

The chat transcript is `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"`: a polite region on a token-by-token stream would read every token. The composer's status line announces the run's state instead, and the transcript is reachable and readable on demand. Declared in the inventory rather than silently left off - making the transcript announce is a bigger behavioural change than this story should carry.
The modal backdrop keeps its `onclick` and takes no tab stop: a click outside the dialog closes it and Escape is the keyboard path. Declared, with the walk proving Escape closes the dialog it opened.

Carried forward: demo tok/s still written to `perf_samples`; `ttft` fixture-equal; `prefill_tps`/`cached_tokens` unprinted; restored checkpoint carries no contract; Hall readiness refresh rewrites seat pickers; `auto_unload` drops just-compared model; browser comparison copy capped at 60,000 chars; `stopped` status carries warn tone; model-residency chips (`LOADED`/`LOADING`) deliberately outside the vocabulary.

`--target-min: 24px` raises the floor, not the whole design: chips, `summary` disclosures, checkbox labels and the permission badge are now 24px tall instead of 18-23px, which makes dense rows about 4-6px taller. That is the visible cost of a finger-sized target and it is deliberate.

The pipeline stepper still overflows horizontally at phone widths; it scrolls rather than wrapping, which keeps the five stages on one line (their order is the point). The walk names it as a scroller instead of excusing it.

Carried forward: demo tok/s still written to `perf_samples`; `ttft` fixture-equal; `prefill_tps`/`cached_tokens` unprinted; restored checkpoint carries no contract; Hall readiness refresh rewrites seat pickers; `auto_unload` drops just-compared model; browser comparison copy capped at 60,000 chars; `stopped` status carries warn tone; model-residency chips (`LOADED`/`LOADING`) deliberately outside the vocabulary; `#chatMessages` stays `aria-live="off"` with its reason declared.
A five-message conversation still pays about 0.7 ms a frame, and a 60-message one about 1 ms: that is the cost of drawing the message being written and it is not hidden.

Once the window is full, an arrival that is not a pure append (an approval changed, a gap forced a resync) still rebuilds the visible window at about 1.5 ms - a bounded cost, paid only when the cards on screen really did change.

The DOM now shows the newest 300 cards and not the whole log. The pane says so, the timeline count names the true total, Replay re-reads everything from the server, and the durable log, cursor and `retained_from_seq` semantics are untouched - but a reader looking for event 4,000 of 5,000 has to use Replay.

The client cache keeps 5,000 events, so a backgrounded tab that returns after more than 5,000 events gets a window rather than the whole log; the gap detection already forced a snapshot reload before this story and still does.

The strip and the window note count what the view holds, not what the log holds: both read `harnessCachedEvents()`, which is bounded at 5,000 events and, after a prune, holds only the retained range - so `9 events held` means this view holds nine over the retained floor, not that the log holds nine. Since #183 the count and the drawn cards cannot disagree (the walk asserts count == cards after a pruned resync), but the number is still the view's. Whether it should name the log's `retained_from_seq`..`latest_seq` instead is an open decision, tracked as #185, and is not claimed here.

The refusal is also announced as a toast with the server's reason (the inline box carries the actions). This is deliberate - a pane behind a backdrop or scrolled away still announces - but it means the same sentence can appear twice when the dialog is open.

Observed, not fixed: the Harness empty state scrolls under the composer at 900px, so the third starter card sits below the fold in the refreshed capture. It is the pane's own focusable scroll region (`.harness-stream { overflow-y: auto }`), not a clip, and fixing the fold would be a pane layout change with its own evidence burden.
22 capture sets carry no `index.json`: their captures cannot be shown to be the bytes their walk produced, only that they exist and that their theme is what their name claims.
The published set has no narrow variant. Narrow coverage comes from `polish`, `responsive`, `uiux-p5-05` and `screenshots/p4-01-narrow-dark` (420x1200), which the review counts under their own sets.

Pre-existing and not this story's: the Python 3.12 CI job failed once on `tests/test_trusted_transformations.py::test_http_endpoints_and_standalone_studio_bundle_parity` (`assert eval_json["ab_gate_passed"] is True`). That gate compares `benefit_justifies_cost`, which includes `overhead_med <= TT_MAX_OVERHEAD_MS_CEILING` measured in wall-clock milliseconds, so a busy runner can fail it; the same test passed in the 3.11 and 3.13 jobs and eight local runs, and this story touches no transformation code. The job was re-run by pushing the ledger edit - not by relaxing the test.

open_risks: The plan was authored from GitHub web extracts, not a local checkout: baseline.readme, baseline.frontend and baseline.roadmap say 'retrieved live', tests say 'not executed', and the backend API contracts were 'not fully audited'. UIUX-P0-01 to P0-06 exist to replace that with measured evidence; until they close, every current-behaviour statement in this ledger is a hypothesis.

Tab labels in this ledger (Start, Harness, Council, Pipeline, Compare, Chat) are NOT the DOM ids in static/index.html (start, harness, hall, council, debate, chat): 'Council' is data-tab=hall and 'Pipeline' is data-tab=council, while data-tab=council is the Pipeline pane. tab_registry records the mapping and tests/test_uiux_roadmap.py fails if it drifts. A session that greps for a 'pipeline' tab will not find one.

static/index.html is a single 4576-line vanilla file with inline script and CSS, and studio.py embeds a regenerated copy. Any story that edits the frontend must run scripts/build_studio.py and let the drift check pass, or the standalone build silently diverges.

Screenshot capture needs a Chrome/Chromium binary and puppeteer-core, neither vendored. Stories that claim visual evidence must capture it on a machine that has them, and must not mark visual evidence as passed when the capture was skipped.

The six panes share one shell, one integration strip and one telemetry rail. A story scoped to one pane can regress another; the feature-preservation matrix is the checklist, and P5-01..P5-03 plus P6-01/P6-02 are the regression gates.

A parallel session owns the optional M5 P6 stories (the lessons/retrieval work). If a UI story surfaces a backend defect, it is recorded as a new M5 story or an open risk, never fixed inside a UI pull request.

The program's prose had drifted from the code at the pin: the program page still said 102 routes and 11 pinned files while app.py mounts 115 and the manifest now pins 12. Counts in docs are re-derived from the artifacts, not remembered.

PR #104 was closed rather than merged: its UIUX-P0-03 work was ported to #109 and landed there, but the runtime-program benchmark diagnostics that branch also carried still need their own pull request in the runtime program.

UIUX-P0-05 cannot be closed in this environment: the six baseline screenshots need Chrome/Chromium and puppeteer-core, neither of which is vendored. The test-results half is capturable here; the visual half needs a machine with a browser, and the owner has said they will capture there.

Two sessions are closing UI/UX stories against the same static/index.html at the same time. P3-01 and the P2-04 work merged without a source conflict because they own different panes, but every generated artifact conflicted: resolve those by regenerating from the merged source rather than by choosing a side, and re-run the full suite on the merged tree, because each story's own numbers describe its own commit.

The demo path's fabricated tok/s figures still reach `perf_samples`: `_stream_omlx_completion` yields 29.5/42.1 for text it wrote itself, `record_perf` stores them, and the throughput card and leaderboard count them. UIUX-P4-01 labels the reply and declines the badge, but it did not change the write, because that is a runtime-program defect and belongs to the M5 stories, not to a UI pull request.

`syncUnifiedSelectors` offers only resident local models, so loading a model rebuilds the catalogue and can re-pick a seat whose model was not in it. The Council readiness row always describes what the round would post, but an operator's earlier pick can change under them; the fix belongs to the model selector, and is recorded rather than patched inside a story about roles and readiness.

A pipeline view restored from the browser's checkpoint carries no contract: the checkpoint payload records what each seat produced, not what it was allowed, so the deliberation evidence table's `Allowed` column is empty after a reload. Widening that payload belongs to the recovery story that owns the format.

`record_perf` still stores the demo path's fabricated 29.5/42.1 tok/s in `perf_samples`; P4-02 removed every drawing of that figure from the Council pane, but the write is the runtime program's to remove.

The preservation suite proves 17 of the 21 matrix rows. The other four sit behind two harness walks that fail on tracked defects #169 and #170; the suite reports them as `known` and never as a pass, which means "the UI is preserved" is a claim with a visible hole in it until those two are fixed in the runtime program.

`product/M5_2_0_UIUX_Preservation_Run.json` is only as current as the last run. A story that lands after it will be described by a record that predates it; re-run `scripts/preservation_suite.py --save` when the tree moves, and do not read a passing record as a statement about a later commit.

the subsystem inventory, rebuilt from the same decorators and their tables

what_this_program_changed: One shell for six panes: a rail, a workspace and an inspector, with the tab registry, the shortcuts and the focus order recorded in `product/M5_2_0_UIUX_Source_Manifest.json`.
One status vocabulary: nine states drawn from six tones, with every surface that speaks it enumerated in `product/M5_2_0_UIUX_Status_Components.json`.
Design tokens as the only place a colour, radius, spacing or motion value is decided, with measured contrast floors (`product/M5_2_0_UIUX_Tokens.json`).
Presentations for the empty, error and recovery cases, hosted rather than re-invented in each pane (`product/M5_2_0_UIUX_Presentations.json`).
Journeys that report what the server actually did: the preflight's next action, durable task state in Harness and Pipeline, Council's deliberation, Compare's provenance, Chat's handoff to Harness.
A preservation harness, an adversarial harness, a screenshot review and a documentation verification, each with its own generator and its own failing mode.
what_held: Endpoints, authorization contracts, approvals, event-cursor semantics, action admission, sandbox controls, workspace edits and session recovery: 21 capabilities across 6 panes, each with a prover, and no route removed.
No new dependency, no CDN, no framework migration, no new outbound request.
Untrusted text stays text: the adversarial inventory maps all 12 refusals and no pane decides authority locally.
where_the_evidence_lives: `product/M5_2_0_UIUX_*.json` - one artifact per story, each with a `--check` mode.
`docs/uiux-2-0-*.md` - one generated page per artifact, plus this gate and this handover.
`docs/media/` - 240 committed captures in 27 sets, reviewed by `uiux_screenshot_review.py`.
CI: `test (3.11)`, `test (3.12)`, `test (3.13)` and `Browser safety regressions` on every push.
what_is_not_claimed: That the interface is beautiful, or that the copy is good: those are the owner's calls.

That every pane was photographed in every theme and width: the coverage grid names the combinations nobody has looked at yet, and they are 0 findings only because they are holes rather than contradictions.
That the program's verdict is the gate's: this file lists evidence with exit codes, and the acceptance verdict belongs to the reviewer.
